:::{#def-polynomial-degree}
#### Degree of a polynomial

Let $f(x) = a_n x^n + \cdots + a_1 x + a_0$
be a [polynomial](#def-polynomial) with $a_n \ne 0$.
The integer $n$ is the **degree** of $f$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-polynomial-degree}
#### Degrees of some polynomials

- $f(x) = 4x$ has degree $1$.
- $f(x) = 5 - 2x^2 + x^3$ has degree $3$:
  the degree is the highest power with a nonzero coefficient,
  not the power in the first term written.
- A constant polynomial $f(x) = 7$ has degree $0$.

:::
